items.title: 18.10.3 Reaction Between Copper(II) Ion and Iodide Ion

source_refs.note: Topic 18.10.3 with Quick Check 18.8, answered (PDF 34). The thiosulphate equation is added for the titration the book mentions. The exercises (PDF 35-37) are not part of the lesson body. Answers need review.

blocks.text: When excess potassium iodide is added to copper(II) sulphate solution, a white precipitate of copper(I) iodide forms in a red-brown solution of iodine: 2Cu2+(aq) + 4I-(aq) -> 2CuI(s) + I2(aq). The half-equations are:

The I2/I- couple has the higher E, so on these values alone it is iodine that should be reduced; the Cu2+/Cu+ couple has the lower E, which suggests Cu+ is a better reducing agent than I-. For the reaction as written, E cell = 0.15 - 0.54 = -0.39 V, which is negative. Yet the reaction goes forward, because the CuI formed keeps precipitating out of solution. This removes the Cu+ product and shifts the equilibrium to the right (Le Chatelier's principle).

blocks.title: Measuring the iodine
blocks.text: The iodine formed can be measured by titration with sodium thiosulphate solution: I2 + 2S2O3 2- -> 2I- + S4O6 2-.

blocks.prompt: State the principle used to decide whether a redox reaction is feasible from standard electrode potentials.
blocks.explanation: Calculate E cell = E(reduction) - E(oxidation); the reaction is feasible if E cell is positive. The species with the more positive E is reduced.

blocks.prompt: For MnO4- (E = +1.52 V) and Fe3+/Fe2+ (E = +0.77 V), identify the oxidising and reducing agents.
blocks.explanation: MnO4- is the oxidising agent (it is reduced to Mn2+); Fe2+ is the reducing agent (it is oxidised to Fe3+).

blocks.prompt: Why is water left out when calculating E cell for the MnO4- and C2O4 2- reaction, though it appears in the equation?
blocks.explanation: E cell is found only from the two standard electrode potentials, which already refer to the complete half-equations under standard conditions; water is the solvent, its amount is effectively constant, and it does not enter the calculation.

items: CuI precipitating removes Cu+ and drives the reaction (Le Chatelier).
The iodine is titrated with thiosulphate.
